flows.description: DF13: createOrder, deleteOrder, and the listOrders poll.
DF12: per-UID draft persistence.
DF05: getMyProfile and updateMyDepartment.
DF04: auth state subscription and ID token refresh.
DF06: fallback profile read, denied by security rules.
DF18: Firebase ID token verification by the callable runtime.
DF17: Admin SDK reads and writes that bypass security rules.
DF15: resumable attachment upload and object deletion.
DF09: enters service line items and attaches files.
DF01: loads the compiled SPA bundle, unauthenticated.
DF16: direct attachment download via an unauthenticated tokenized URL.
DF02: credentials entry.
DF08: browses requests and version history.
DF11: submits, withdraws, approves, or rejects a request.
DF10: reviews computed pricing and confirms the request.
DF07: SDK initialisation from build-time-injected config.
DF03: email and password sign-in exchange.
DF21: bulk read and rewrite of every order document.
DF20: deploys the bundle, Firestore rules, and Storage rules.
DF19: runs the migration script from a workstation shell.
DF14: submitForApproval, withdrawFromReview, approveOrder, rejectOrder.

threats.title: Abuse — delete wrapper carries no role condition
threats.description: handleDeleteOrder is a plain callable wrapper whose visibility is decided only by the UI.
threats.mitigation: deleteOrder re-resolves the caller role server-side and rejects non-admins.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unconditional four-second poll per tab
threats.description: Each open tab mounts a 4s listOrders poll with no backoff, multiplying backend read volume.
threats.mitigation: Add backoff and pagination, pause when hidden, and enforce App Check plus rate limits.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — client-only route guards
threats.description: RequireUser restricts the entry route in the browser only and can be bypassed.
threats.mitigation: createOrder independently rejects any caller whose server-resolved role is not user.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — cleartext draft in localStorage
threats.description: Draft services and metadata persist in localStorage in cleartext and are never cleared on sign-out.
threats.mitigation: Clear both keys on logout and stop persisting cost-bearing fields.

threats.title: Tampering — bypassable client route guards
threats.description: RequireAuth, RequireUser and BlockViewer run in the browser and are bypassable by editing the bundle.
threats.mitigation: Every guard is duplicated server-side inside the callables.

threats.title: Tampering — duplicate copies authority and financing fields
threats.description: handleDuplicateOrder copies finalDecisionAuthorityRank and financing totals into a fresh draft.
threats.mitigation: createOrder strips the rank and recomputes every financing figure from the line items.

threats.title: Denial of Service — profile failure silently downgrades role
threats.description: A getMyProfile failure falls through to a denied Firestore read and then assigns role user.
threats.mitigation: Surface the failure and retry rather than defaulting to a role.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — direct Firestore profile fallback
threats.description: The fallback path would accept whatever role a client-read users document asserts.
threats.mitigation: firestore.rules denies all client reads of users, so the fallback cannot succeed.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — role and errors logged to console
threats.description: The resolved role and raw error objects are written to the browser console.
threats.mitigation: Strip identity and role details from production console output.

threats.title: Spoofing — approver identity from an email substring
threats.description: getMyProfile returns rank4 for any unprovisioned caller whose email contains that substring.
threats.mitigation: Return only roles backed by a provisioned users document.

threats.title: Tampering — optimistic department update never reverted
threats.description: updateDepartment sets local state before the callable and does not roll back on rejection.
threats.mitigation: Apply the change only after the callable resolves and re-read the profile on failure.

threats.title: Abuse — non-transactional approval race
threats.description: approveOrder and rejectOrder read then update outside a transaction, allowing lost audit entries.
threats.mitigation: Wrap read, checks and write in db.runTransaction and append history with arrayUnion.

threats.title: Abuse — unlimited withdraw and resubmit re-roll
threats.description: The creator can withdraw mid-chain and resubmit, restarting at Rank 4 with history cleared.
threats.mitigation: Preserve history across withdrawal, record re-submissions, and notify prior approvers.

threats.title: Abuse — unbounded contractPeriod into the PMT formula
threats.description: The contractPeriod fallback accepts any floored client integer and drives the financing lease.
threats.mitigation: Bound contractPeriod to the INSTALLMENT_PERIODS enumeration.

threats.title: Denial of Service — full collection read per listOrders call
threats.description: listOrders reads every order document on every call with no pagination or rate limit.
threats.mitigation: Use indexed paginated queries, enable App Check, and add per-caller rate limiting.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unbounded order creation
threats.description: createOrder can be looped by any Requester, inflating cost and consuming FA numbers.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit creation per caller and per time window.

threats.title: Denial of Service — approval comment length unbounded
threats.description: approveOrder and rejectOrder require a non-empty comment but apply no maximum length.
threats.mitigation: Bound the comment to a documented maximum and reject longer input with invalid-argument.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — unprovisioned callers default to Requester
threats.description: getCallerProfile returns role user when no profile document exists, granting write access.
threats.mitigation: Default unprovisioned principals to a no-privilege role and reject them explicitly.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — admin satisfies every rank check
threats.description: The admin role adopts the pending rank, so one identity can approve the whole chain.
threats.mitigation: Record overrides distinctly and prevent one identity satisfying multiple ranks.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — viewer strip list misses derived cost
threats.description: ORDER_SENSITIVE_FIELDS lists only totalCost, leaving totalOneTimeChargeB2S in the viewer response.
threats.mitigation: Build the viewer projection from an allow-list rather than a deny-list.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Rank 4 department filter fails open
threats.description: listOrders matches every order when the approver or the order has no department value.
threats.mitigation: Reuse the fail-closed canAccessOrder helper for the read path.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — version expansion by order number
threats.description: listOrders re-filters by orderNumber, returning versions the approver was never routed.
threats.mitigation: Apply the per-document scope rule to history as well as the current version.

threats.title: Repudiation — no security event logging
threats.description: No callable records creation, approval, rejection, withdrawal or deletion anywhere.
threats.mitigation: Write append-only auditLog entries from every state-changing callable.

threats.title: Repudiation — hard delete removes the audit trail
threats.description: deleteOrder removes the document and its embedded approvalHistory with no tombstone.
threats.mitigation: Soft-delete with retention and write an audit entry before the state change.

threats.title: Spoofing — viewer scope from a free-text name
threats.description: Viewer access is decided by matching the typed accountManager string to the profile name.
threats.mitigation: Key viewer scope to a stable UID or verified email recorded at creation time.

threats.title: Spoofing — dual profile keys can disagree
threats.description: getCallerProfile reads users/{uid} then users/{email}; the two documents may carry different roles.
threats.mitigation: Resolve profiles by UID only and migrate email-keyed documents.

threats.title: Tampering — client controls orderNumber, version and createdAt
threats.description: Three identity-bearing fields pass through createOrder unstripped and unvalidated.
threats.mitigation: Make all three server-owned and verify a supplied orderNumber belongs to the caller.

threats.title: Tampering — submitForApproval clears approvalHistory
threats.description: The submit handler writes an empty approvalHistory array, discarding recorded decisions.
threats.mitigation: Append a resubmission marker and move the trail to an append-only subcollection.

threats.title: Tampering — attachment metadata written unvalidated
threats.description: Every attachment field including url and path is stored exactly as the caller supplied it.
threats.mitigation: Validate path against the caller prefix and reconstruct the link server-side.

threats.title: Tampering — unpinned function runtime dependencies
threats.description: functions/ has no package.json or lockfile, so firebase-admin and firebase-functions are unpinned.
threats.mitigation: Add functions/package.json with pinned versions, commit the lockfile, assert the floor in CI.

threats.title: Abuse — dangling URL after attachment removal
threats.description: Removing an attachment deletes the object but persisted orders keep the URL.
threats.mitigation: Freeze attachments at submission by copying to an immutable order-scoped prefix.

threats.title: Denial of Service — no attachment count or total quota
threats.description: Nothing limits how many attachments a requester uploads or their cumulative size.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-user quotas and expire orphaned draft objects by lifecycle rule.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — tokenized URL persisted on the order
threats.description: getDownloadURL output is stored in the draft and later on the order document.
threats.mitigation: Closed by FIND-01 (2026-09-23): getDownloadURL removed, only the path stored, signed URL minted after authorization.

threats.title: Tampering — upload content type is client-declared and never verified
threats.description: Both the browser check and the storage.rules check read the same client-declared content type, so neither verifies the bytes; any payload can be uploaded labelled application/pdf.
threats.mitigation: Verify content server-side by magic-byte inspection in a post-upload function and treat the declared content type as untrusted.

threats.title: Tampering — client and rules size limits disagree
threats.description: The browser applies one 100 MB ceiling to both types while storage.rules caps PDFs at 5 MB.
threats.mitigation: Make the client limits per-type and derive both sides from one shared constant.

threats.title: Abuse — unverified email addresses accepted
threats.description: The email claim stamped into createdBy and approvedBy is never verified as controlled by the holder.
threats.mitigation: Gate sign-in on email_verified in a blocking authentication function.

identity_key.attack_surface: Identity Platform sign-in, no email_verified check

threats.title: Denial of Service — sign-in flooding and account lockout
threats.description: Repeated attempts against a known address can exhaust or lock the account.
threats.mitigation: Firebase Authentication applies per-IP and per-account throttling with CAPTCHA escalation.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — rank4 granted from an email substring
threats.description: getMyProfile grants the rank4 role and a department from substrings of the email address.
threats.mitigation: Remove the substring heuristics and resolve only from provisioned users documents.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — stale privileges for the ID token lifetime
threats.description: ID tokens are never checked for revocation, so a deprovisioned account keeps a usable session until expiry.
threats.mitigation: Check revocation via verifyIdToken(token, true) in the callables and revoke refresh tokens on deprovisioning.

identity_key.attack_surface: functions/src/index.ts request.auth with no revocation check

threats.title: Information Disclosure — account enumeration
threats.description: Identity Toolkit responses can distinguish registered from unregistered addresses.
threats.mitigation: Firebase email-enumeration protection is a project-level setting applied by the platform.

threats.title: Spoofing — no identity-provider restriction
threats.description: No blocking function, domain allow-list or verification gate restricts which identities are valid.
threats.mitigation: Add a beforeSignIn blocking function enforcing the corporate domain and a verified email.

threats.title: Spoofing — no multi-factor authentication
threats.description: Accounts authorising financial commitments are protected by a password alone.
threats.mitigation: Require multi-factor enrolment for every rank-holding and admin account.

threats.title: Repudiation — sign-in records not retained or surfaced
threats.description: Identity Platform sign-in logs are never exported or correlated with approval events.
threats.mitigation: Export Identity Platform audit logs to a retained sink and correlate with approvals.

identity_key.attack_surface: No log export configuration in the repository

threats.title: Abuse — project config embedded in the public bundle
threats.description: The Firebase web config is compiled into the bundle, letting anyone address the endpoints.
threats.mitigation: This is the documented Firebase web model; callables require a verified ID token and rules deny direct access.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — identity attributes in thrown errors
threats.description: handleFirestoreError serialises uid, email, tenantId and provider data into a logged and thrown message.
threats.mitigation: Log a correlation id instead and keep identity attributes out of thrown messages.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — dev server binds all interfaces
threats.description: The dev script starts Vite with --host=0.0.0.0, exposing the development build and source maps to the local network.
threats.mitigation: Bind the dev server to 127.0.0.1 and require an explicit opt-in flag for LAN exposure.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — GEMINI_API_KEY inlined on first reference
threats.description: vite.config.ts defines a substitution for the secret, so it ships to the browser the moment any file references the identifier; nothing references it today.
threats.mitigation: Delete the define entry and the unused @google/genai dependency; hold the key server-side if Gemini is added.

threats.title: Tampering — optional database id could diverge from the functions
threats.description: The client falls through to the implicit default database while the functions pin (default).
threats.mitigation: Both paths converge on (default) and firebase.json deploys the same ruleset to both databases.

threats.title: Tampering — build-time config file can repoint the application
threats.description: vite.config.ts reads firebase-applet-config.json when present and uses it to supply the Firebase project configuration.
threats.mitigation: Remove the file-based fallback, or require an explicit opt-in flag and assert the resolved project id at build time.

threats.title: Abuse — catch-all rewrite exposes the full route surface
threats.description: Every path returns index.html, so any URL renders the application shell.
threats.mitigation: Required SPA routing; all data access is authorized server-side so reaching a route yields no data.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unauthenticated bundle serving
threats.description: The bundle is served to unauthenticated clients so request volume is unbounded.
threats.mitigation: Firebase Hosting fronts the content with Google's CDN, which absorbs volumetric load.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — no Referrer-Policy header
threats.description: Tokenized attachment URLs can leak to third-party hosts through the Referer header.
threats.mitigation: Set Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin in the hosting headers.

identity_key.attack_surface: firebase.json hosting block, no headers key

threats.title: Spoofing — clickjacking of the approval control
threats.description: No CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, so the approval screen can be framed and clicks redirected.
threats.mitigation: Add a headers block with frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY.

identity_key.attack_surface: firebase.json hosting block, no headers key

threats.title: Tampering — no CSP script-src or subresource integrity
threats.description: An injected script would execute with the signed-in user's full session authority.
threats.mitigation: Ship a restrictive script-src policy and pin third-party assets with integrity hashes.

identity_key.attack_surface: firebase.json hosting block, no headers key

threats.title: Abuse — attachment swapped after approver review
threats.description: Attachments are never re-validated at submission, so the object behind a URL can be replaced.
threats.mitigation: Copy attachments to an immutable order-scoped prefix at submission and block writes there.

threats.title: Denial of Service — no aggregate storage quota
threats.description: Per-object limits exist but nothing bounds object count or total bytes per user.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-user quotas and lifecycle rules expiring orphaned draft objects.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — link possession is the effective authorization
threats.description: Rules give approvers no read path, so the unauthenticated token URL is the only working access.
threats.mitigation: Closed by FIND-01 (2026-09-23): getAttachmentUrl authorizes with the getOrder predicate minus viewers before signing.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — unauthenticated tokenized download URLs
threats.description: getDownloadURL tokens serve the object to anyone holding the link, outliving order authorization.
threats.mitigation: Closed by FIND-01 (2026-09-23): no tokens minted; the 10 previously-issued tokens were revoked.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — original filenames rendered to all readers
threats.description: Filenames embedded in the object path disclose customer, vendor and deal names.
threats.mitigation: Not closed by FIND-01; split out as FIND-37. Store a generated object name, keep the display name under the order's scope rules, and bring attachments under stripForViewer.

threats.title: Tampering — stored url never checked against the Storage origin
threats.description: The displayed link need not point at the uploaded object or match the sibling path field.
threats.mitigation: Reconstruct the link server-side from the validated path and ignore the client url.

threats.title: Abuse — FA counter permanently consumed and never reconciled
threats.description: counters/orders increments monotonically with no reconciliation against the collection.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit creation and reconcile the counter against the collection periodically.

threats.title: Denial of Service — read cost grows linearly with history
threats.description: Every listOrders call reads the whole collection while clients poll every four seconds.
threats.mitigation: Add indexed paginated queries scoped by role so the read set is bounded.

threats.title: Denial of Service — approvalHistory grows toward the document limit
threats.description: The inline approvalHistory array grows per decision toward Firestore's 1 MB ceiling, past which every write to that order fails.
threats.mitigation: Move the trail to an auditLog subcollection and cap comment length.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — direct client writes to users or orders
threats.description: Client writes to these collections would let any signed-in user grant themselves a role.
threats.mitigation: firestore.rules sets allow read, write: if false on all three collections plus a catch-all deny.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — Admin SDK holds unrestricted project-wide access
threats.description: All callables share one service account with project-wide Firestore access, and the Admin SDK bypasses security rules, so any single defect reaches every collection.
threats.mitigation: Run the callables under a dedicated service account scoped to the collections they use, and split by privilege.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — plaintext commercial data returned whole
threats.description: Order documents hold customer, cost and margin data returned entirely to any in-scope caller.
threats.mitigation: Split cost-bearing fields into a separately authorized subcollection.

threats.title: Repudiation — no audit export or point-in-time recovery
threats.description: No Firestore audit-log export, retention policy or PITR configuration exists in the repository.
threats.mitigation: Enable Firestore PITR and export Data Access audit logs to a retained sink.

threats.title: Tampering — no schema enforcement, undefined fields dropped silently
threats.description: ignoreUndefinedProperties causes malformed fields to be dropped rather than rejected.
threats.mitigation: Validate the full order shape server-side against the declared types before writing.

threats.title: Abuse — per-UID drafts accumulate on shared workstations
threats.description: Keys are namespaced per UID but never expired, so every account leaves a readable draft.
threats.mitigation: Remove other users' keys on sign-in and clear the current user's on sign-out.

threats.title: Denial of Service — storage quota exhaustion breaks the render
threats.description: Accumulated drafts can exhaust the origin quota and the unguarded setItem call throws.
threats.mitigation: Wrap writes in try/catch, cap draft size, and evict stale per-UID keys.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — cost data readable after sign-out
threats.description: Company, brief, cost per unit, buffer and margin persist in cleartext and survive logout.
threats.mitigation: Clear both keys on logout and stop persisting cost-bearing fields.

threats.title: Tampering — restored draft parsed back with no integrity check
threats.description: Anything able to write the key controls the next request the user submits.
threats.mitigation: Treat restored drafts as untrusted input and re-validate on load.

threats.title: Abuse — any email domain accepted at sign-in
threats.description: The corporate domain appears only as a placeholder; nothing restricts external identities.
threats.mitigation: Enforce the corporate domain in a blocking authentication function, not in UI copy.

threats.title: Denial of Service — no client throttling or CAPTCHA
threats.description: The form applies no rate limiting to repeated sign-in attempts.
threats.mitigation: Firebase Authentication applies per-IP and per-account throttling with CAPTCHA escalation.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — sign-in failure could reveal registration
threats.description: A per-cause error message would distinguish an unknown address from a wrong password.
threats.mitigation: The catch block sets one generic message for every failure mode.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — password toggle renders the credential into the DOM
threats.description: The reveal control switches the input to type=text with no timeout or revert, exposing the live credential as readable DOM text.
threats.mitigation: Auto-revert to masked after a short timeout and on blur and submit.

threats.title: Spoofing — single-factor credentials only
threats.description: The form collects an email and a password with no second factor or step-up challenge.
threats.mitigation: Add multi-factor enrolment and a step-up challenge before approval actions.

threats.title: Abuse — duplicate copies another user's order into a draft
threats.description: The duplicate control copies any listed order, including one created by another user.
threats.mitigation: Restrict duplication to orders the caller created and enforce it in createOrder.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — admin-only delete control is a client check
threats.description: The trash control renders on a client-side role === admin comparison.
threats.mitigation: deleteOrder repeats the admin check server-side from the resolved profile.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — over-broad server scope surfaced directly
threats.description: Created By and the full version history render whatever listOrders returned.
threats.mitigation: Fix the server scope; the client must not be the control that limits what is shown.

threats.title: Denial of Service — sequential rewrite contends for write quota
threats.description: A per-document await over the whole collection competes with live traffic as history grows.
threats.mitigation: Use batched writes with bounded concurrency during a maintenance window.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — runs under Application Default Credentials
threats.description: A bare initializeApp picks up credentials that typically carry project-owner scope.
threats.mitigation: Run under a dedicated service account limited to the orders collection.

threats.title: Repudiation — rewrites carry no marker and only console output
threats.description: Migrated fields are indistinguishable from user edits and the run leaves no durable record.
threats.mitigation: Stamp a migration id and timestamp per document and write a run record to the audit collection.

threats.title: Tampering — bulk rewrite with no dry-run, backup or confirmation
threats.description: The script rewrites every matching order document with no safety step and no scoping query.
threats.mitigation: Make dry-run the default, export first, and query only documents matching the old values.

threats.title: Abuse — withdraw discards collected approvals
threats.description: The creator can pull an approved-in-part request back to Draft and restart the chain.
threats.mitigation: Preserve and display prior decisions across withdrawal and notify approvers who signed off.

threats.title: Abuse — order id taken from the query string
threats.description: The displayed order is selected by an id the user can set to any document id.
threats.mitigation: Lookup runs over the already-authorized listOrders result, so an out-of-scope id renders not found.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — approver controls gated client-side
threats.description: isAuthorizedApprover decides whether the Approve and Reject controls render.
threats.mitigation: approveOrder and rejectOrder repeat the rank and department checks and fail closed.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — financial cards gated only in the client
threats.description: The server returns the underlying figures to every non-viewer role regardless of what renders.
threats.mitigation: Project the response per role on the server so the client never receives hidden figures.

threats.title: Repudiation — rendered audit log is cleared on resubmission
threats.description: The panel renders approvalHistory, which submitForApproval clears despite the UI's promise.
threats.mitigation: Preserve history across withdrawal and resubmission in an append-only store.

threats.title: Tampering — direct Firestore write imports remain
threats.description: doc and updateDoc are imported, leaving a direct client write path one line from reintroduction.
threats.mitigation: firestore.rules denies all client writes; remove the unused imports to keep it that way.

threats.title: Abuse — unbounded version growth driven by the client
threats.description: Re-confirming always writes a new document whose client-chosen version decides which is current.
threats.mitigation: Derive version server-side from existing documents for that order number.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — full costing and margin tables rendered
threats.description: The screen renders complete costing, margin and commission figures.
threats.mitigation: BlockViewer keeps viewers off the route and the server projection strips the cost fields.

threats.title: Tampering — client assembles the full order object
threats.description: The screen builds id, version, createdAt and every financing figure and sends them to createOrder.
threats.mitigation: Make version and createdAt server-owned alongside the financial fields already recomputed.

threats.title: Tampering — editing an order discards its attachments
threats.description: The effect that loads an existing order into metadata omits attachments, so re-confirming persists a version with none.
threats.mitigation: Carry attachments through the reload and have createOrder refuse to drop attachments present on the superseded version.

threats.title: Tampering — client proposes the FA order number
threats.description: When none is set the client scans visible orders for the highest FA-NNNN and proposes the next.
threats.mitigation: Make the counter transaction the sole source of order numbers on every path.

No identity-provider restriction on account provisioning or sign-in

Firebase Hosting serves the application without security response headers
